title: An Autonomous, Preregistered Evaluation of a Deterministic Provenance‑Scoring Judge for LLM NetOps "No‑Issue" Assertions
abstract: We evaluate whether a deterministic provenance+validator judge (retrieval grounding, syntactic/semantic validators, telemetry cross‑checks) reduces unsupported LLM "no‑issue" (reachability/health‑holds) assertions in scripted NetOps emulator scenarios. Following a machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) we ran a paired confirmatory execution with gpt-5-mini across 90 seeded tasks (planned 180 episodes). Execution completed 166 episodes (14 failed) yielding 83 complete paired tasks. Baseline (LLM only) success: 81/83 (97.59%); guarded (judge) success: 83/83 (100.0%). Absolute paired improvement = 0.0240963855; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.000, 0.0602409639] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). McNemar two‑sided exact p = 0.50. The guarded pipeline changed two discordant pairs in this synthetic setting; the improvement is numerically small and statistically inconclusive given realized sample size. All execution artifacts and SHA256 digests are recorded in the run manifest and form the authoritative reproducible record for this study. Conclusions are explicitly bounded to the preregistered synthetic/emulator domain.

sections.introduction: LLMs are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks (intent translation, diagnosis, limited self‑healing). A recurring operational hazard is a fluent model assertion that “no issue” (e.g., reachability holds) without programmatic grounding: an unsupported "no‑issue" assertion can silence investigation or trigger unsafe automation. We study whether a deterministic, programmatic judge that enforces retrieval grounding, syntactic/semantic validators, and telemetry cross‑checks can reduce unsupported "no‑issue" assertions in a controlled, preregistered emulator setting. Our manuscript reports a fully preregistered pipeline (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1), the autonomous execution manifest (hashed artifacts), and the preregistered paired confirmatory analysis. The final research contribution is a bounded, evidence‑grounded assessment of the judge architecture under synthetic/emulator conditions and the audited numeric outcome.
sections.related_work: We position this study within generate–validate–repair and tool‑augmented mitigation literature for high‑stakes LLM applications, and NetOps/AIOps work arguing that operational reliability depends on layered tooling, evidence traces, and assurance contracts rather than models alone. Representative leads informing design and interpretation include recent surveys and procedural proposals for retrieval grounding, validator ensembles, and generate→validate pipelines (see cited_record_ids). Our study differs by (i) preregistering a machine‑readable paired confirmatory design, (ii) executing an autonomous run with exhaustive artifact hashing, and (iii) reporting a fully auditable paired inference on scripted NetOps emulator scenarios.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design: The preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1) froze the research question, paired baseline/guarded design, seeds, retry/replacement rules (up to two deterministic retries), task bank (90 seeded emulator scenarios), episode budget (180), model (gpt-5-mini), adapter family (hosted_netops_gvr_v1), primary/secondary estimands, and analysis plan. Judge architecture (frozen): deterministic retrieval grounding (snapshot index), syntactic/semantic validators for generated artifacts, and telemetry cross‑checks against deterministic emulator state. Execution policy: each task run twice (baseline: LLM only; guarded: LLM + judge); deterministic parser extracted the canonical single "no‑issue/reachability holds" assertion per episode for scoring; emulator ground truth provided programmatic supported/unsupported labels. Failure handling: two automatic retries for emulator/parser failures; deterministic replacements from a seeded scenario list when required (manifest logs all replacements). Scoring & analysis (frozen): paired contingency analysis, paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729), and McNemar exact test for paired discordance. All raw responses, provider_call logs, scoring JSONs, and SHA256 digests are recorded in the execution manifest; those files are the authoritative reproducible artifacts for this run.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned episodes 180; completed episodes 166; failed episodes 14; complete paired tasks = 83. Provider/model calls: hosted_model_call_event_count = 92; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7 (detailed provider_call JSONs and hashes in the manifest). Confirmatory paired contingency (n=83 pairs): n_11 (both success) = 81; n_10 (guarded success only) = 2; n_01 (baseline success only) = 0; n_00 = 0. Derived metrics: baseline success rate = 81/83 = 0.9759036144578314; guarded success rate = 83/83 = 1.0; absolute paired improvement = 0.02409638554216864. Paired bootstrap 95% CI (percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729): [0.000, 0.060240963855421686]. McNemar exact two‑sided p = 0.50. Interpretation: the guarded judge changed two discordant pairs in these scripted scenarios; the observed absolute improvement is small and the paired inference is statistically inconclusive at α=0.05 given realized n.
sections.discussion: Bounded interpretation. In a fully preregistered, audited emulator setting, deterministic provenance+validator checks altered a small number of baseline "no‑issue" outcomes (2/83 pairs). This provides limited evidence that layered deterministic gates can change some unsupported assertions in synthetic scenarios; it does not establish production readiness, cross‑model generality, or efficacy on real telemetry. Threats to validity: (1) internal — prompt sensitivity, hosted provider nondeterminism, parser fragility, and missingness from failed episodes; (2) construct — programmatic emulator labels may not capture the richness of production evidence; (3) external — single model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic/emulator scenarios only; (4) conclusion validity — realized paired n=83 reduces power for small effects (the bootstrap CI includes zero and McNemar p=0.50). Deviations and operational notes. The run adhered to the preregistered deterministic retry/replacement policy; 14 episodes failed after retries. Model‑call budget: planned maximum_model_calls = 180, model_calls_used = 92; discrepancy arises from guarded short‑circuiting and failed provider calls (manifest documents per‑call behavior). Reproducibility and audit trail. All raw outputs, scoring JSONs, provider_call logs, seeds, and SHA256 digests are enumerated in the execution manifest produced by the autonomous run (execution/artifact_hashes). The manifest is the authoritative artifact record; no synthesized repository URL is invented here. Practical implication. A deterministic evidence‑gating layer is a plausible engineering control that may reduce some unsupported "no‑issue" assertions, but operators should not treat the present numerical result as proof of effectiveness in production. Larger, multi‑model, and production‑telemetry evaluations are required.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, autonomous paired study testing a deterministic provenance+validator judge against an LLM baseline across scripted NetOps emulator scenarios. In 83 complete paired tasks the guarded judge produced two discordant improvements over the baseline (absolute paired improvement 0.0240963855; 95% paired bootstrap CI = [0.000, 0.0602409639]; McNemar p = 0.50). The numeric change is small and statistically inconclusive at the realized sample size. The bounded conclusion: deterministic, programmatic evidence gating can change a modest number of unsupported LLM "no‑issue" assertions in controlled emulator settings, but broader claims (cross‑model effectiveness or production readiness) are not supported by this run. All execution artifacts and SHA256 digests are recorded in the run manifest and compose the authoritative reproducible record for this study.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed under the CNSM 2026 Agentic AI Researcher requirements with an autonomy lock and a machine‑readable preregistration (cand-2026-003-provenance-prereg-v1). Human roles prior to the autonomy lock: the Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary and Master Prompt v1. After the lock the autonomous system performed literature review, final research selection, the machine‑readable preregistration, code generation, experiment orchestration, model calls, deterministic parsing/scoring, statistical analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and autonomous revision. LLMs and orchestration: the hosted LLM used for the confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini (model identifier recorded in execution/model_configuration.json); the orchestration/adapter family frozen in the preregistration was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt: the immutable Master Prompt v1 was supplied in the frozen input bundle and used to seed autonomous behavior. Prompts, prompt templates, and judge logic (retrieval grounding + syntactic/semantic validators + telemetry cross‑checks) were frozen in the preregistration. Preregistration freeze: the preregistration fixed task bank size (90 seeded emulator scenarios), paired design, seeds, retry/replacement rules (up to two deterministic retries), maximum_model_calls (180), stopping rules, primary and secondary estimands, and the analysis plan. Execution artifacts and provenance: all raw LLM responses, provider_call logs, scoring JSONs, seeds, and per‑file SHA256 digests are recorded in the execution manifest (execution/artifact_hashes) produced by the autonomous run; the manifest paths and digests are the authoritative artifact record. The autonomous run did not produce a single consolidated public repository URL among its artifacts; consequently no repository URL is provided here. Technical restarts and deviations: the run followed the preregistered deterministic retry policy and replacement policy; 14 episodes failed after retries and the completed episode count was 166 (complete paired tasks = 83). Model call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 92; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 7 (details in execution/provider_calls/*.json). No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Limitations declared: experiments used synthetic/emulator scenarios only; single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) limits model generality; realized paired n=83 reduces statistical power; preregistered secondary analyses and ablations were not fully executed and remain unresolved for this run. The Research Director reviewed and approved the design before the autonomy lock; all subsequent scientific decisions, execution steps, analyses, and manuscript text were produced autonomously and logged in the autonomous revision and execution records.
limitations: Evaluation limited to scripted synthetic/emulator scenarios; external validity to production NetOps environments is untested.
Single‑model experiment (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or versions.
Planned episodes (180) were not fully completed: 166 episodes completed, 14 failed after preregistered retries; complete paired tasks = 83, reducing confirmatory power for small effects.

Preregistered primary estimand was F1 on a held‑out split; realized execution produced paired episodes and the confirmatory analysis used a paired contingency/McNemar framework to preserve within‑task counterfactuals — this analytic change is declared and justified but represents a deviation from the original estimand.

Preregistered secondary metrics and ablations (precision/recall with bootstrap CIs, Brier/calibration, retrieval/telemetry/validator ablations) were not fully executed to completion on the realized paired dataset and are therefore unresolved for this run.

Provider/model call budget discrepancy: planned maximum_model_calls = 180 vs model_calls_used = 92 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 85); the manifest records short‑circuiting, guarded early exits, and failed calls that explain the discrepancy but the episode→call mapping is not one‑to‑one.
Construct validity: the supported/unsupported labels derive from emulator ground truth and may not reflect production telemetry or evidence modalities.
